title: Add batching_tier request option (header) for workload-aware batching defaults
author: Wei Chen
description:
Context: Runtime is shipping tiered workload-aware batching defaults (fast / standard / cost-efficient). Customers need an SDK-level way to explicitly pick a tier (or keep server defaults) without reaching into manual batching knobs. This PR adds an optional `batching_tier` parameter across request surfaces and sends it as an HTTP header for the control plane/runtime to interpret.

What’s in this PR: 1) Client option: add `batching_tier: Optional[str]` (and typed Literal where available) on generation endpoints (chat + completions + embeddings where applicable, though runtime will ignore for non-generation). 2) Transport: serialize `batching_tier` into header `X-Redwood-Batching-Tier` with wire values: `fast`, `standard`, `cost-efficient`. 3) Validation: reject invalid values client-side with a clear error message; allow None/unspecified. Also normalize `cost_efficient` -> `cost-efficient` for ergonomics (accept both on input, always send `cost-efficient`). 4) Docs: add usage examples and a short FAQ note explaining that tier selection affects scheduling/batching behavior only (no change to logging/retention). 5) Changelog: add an entry under Unreleased.

Why header vs body: We already use headers for request-level policy hints (e.g., tracing/debug flags). Keeping this as a header avoids changes to multiple request schemas and makes it easy to apply consistently across endpoints.

Backwards compatibility: Default remains unchanged. If `batching_tier` is not set, the SDK sends nothing and the service selects the default tier per route/model policy.

Example:
- Python: `client.chat.completions.create(model="redwood/llama-3.1-70b", messages=[...], batching_tier="fast")`
- Wire header: `X-Redwood-Batching-Tier: fast`

Notes / follow-ups: - We intentionally do not expose manual batching knobs in the SDK in this PR; tier selection is the supported surface. - Dedicated override precedence is handled server-side (customer override > route policy > tier default); this PR just passes the requested tier.

Testing: - Unit tests for validation + normalization. - VCR-style integration test verifies header is present. - Lint + mypy.

Release note (SDK): Add `batching_tier` parameter to select workload-aware batching tier (fast/standard/cost-efficient).
commits: sdk: add BatchingTier type + validation helper
client: plumb batching_tier through request options and send X-Redwood-Batching-Tier header
tests: add unit + transport coverage for tier header + normalization
review_conversation:
Henry Cho (review): Can we avoid accepting arbitrary strings? Prefer a typed enum/Literal to reduce support issues. Also please clarify docs that choosing a tier is a latency/cost trade-off and not an SLA guarantee.

Wei Chen (author): Added `BatchingTier = Literal["fast","standard","cost-efficient"]` plus input normalization for `cost_efficient` (common python style). Invalid values now raise `ValueError` with the allowed set. Updated docs language to avoid SLA wording.

Jordan Lee (review): Header name/value: runtime expects `X-Redwood-Batching-Tier` and value `cost-efficient` (hyphen). Please ensure we always send hyphenated form even if user passes underscore.

Wei Chen (author): Implemented normalization: accept `cost_efficient`/`cost-efficient`, always serialize as `cost-efficient`. Added tests asserting exact header values.

Allison Grant (review): Minor: please add a note that tier selection is included as a label in some metrics/traces server-side; SDK shouldn’t promise visibility. Also consider whether high-cardinality concerns apply.

Wei Chen (author): Added a short note: “tier may appear in server-side telemetry” without promising a specific dashboard view. No client-side cardinality changes.

Henry Cho (final): Looks good. Thanks for keeping this backwards compatible and consistent with the TS SDK plan. Approved.

Merge: Squash merged.
release_notes: SDK: Add `batching_tier` request option (fast/standard/cost-efficient) that sets `X-Redwood-Batching-Tier` header for workload-aware batching defaults.
